_about: Mark's operations tools: dashboard app + token gate, social pipeline, finance, YouTube/Search Console, AI visibility, ops manager, group bookings and group marketing. Checks: e2e/checks/ops.mjs. Every gap below still has its refusal paths (400/401/404/409) exercised on dev by ops.social-writes-refuse, ops.group-writes-refuse, ops.group-marketing-writes-refuse or ops.calendar-conflicts; what is missing is the successful write.

extra.ext:dashboard-app: Mark's dashboard single-page app: https://dashboard.stillafloatcruising.com (password-protected) on prod, http://<dev>/dashboard/ on dev — its index page and main program bundle
extra.ext:ops-manager-health: The SAF ops-manager service (FastAPI webhook app: finance, calendar conflicts, Gmail, YouTube/Search Console analytics) — GET /health on port 5000 (prod) / 5001 (dev), and its x-api-key refusal

GET /api/ops/gsc/insights.reason: Every request makes an uncached model call (ops-manager agent/seo_insights.generate_insights: local box, Anthropic fallback = paid). Only its 401 without the token is checked (ops.auth-gate). Needs a cached or dry-run mode before a sweep may call it.

POST /api/ops/gsc/insights/run.reason: Runs the paid SEO model analysis and files tasks/proposals. Only the 401 without a token is checked (ops.social-writes-refuse). Needs a dry-run flag that analyses nothing and files nothing.

POST /api/ops/resolve-conflict.reason: A successful resolve acts on Mark's real Google Calendar and clears the pending conflict. The unknown-key 404 and the 401 are checked on dev (ops.calendar-conflicts); a success needs a fixture conflict on a test calendar.

POST /api/ai-visibility/activity.reason: A successful POST prepends an entry to Mark's real AI-visibility activity log and there is no delete route, so a fixture could never be removed. Bad kind / missing title (400) and no token (401) are checked on dev (ops.social-writes-refuse).

POST /api/social/ingest.reason: A successful POST appends a snapshot to the live follower-stats series (no delete route). The array-body 400 and the 401 are checked on dev. This key is defined in BOTH social.ts and social-analytics.ts; only social.ts's runs (see site problem: the dashboard's social panel snapshot is never written).

POST /api/social/generate.reason: Generates hooks with a paid model call and notifies Mark. The missing-fields 400 is checked on dev (ops.social-writes-refuse).

POST /api/social/scan.reason: Generates batches for new uploads with paid model calls and notifies Mark. Only the 401 without a token is checked.

POST /api/social/regenerate.reason: Regenerates every hook in the queue with paid model calls, replacing the queue, and notifies Mark. Only the 401 without a token is checked.

POST /api/social/queue/:id/:action.reason: Approve schedules real Facebook/Instagram posts (or posts now); reject changes a real batch; a fixture batch can only be created through the paid generate call. The unknown-action 400 and unknown-batch 404 are checked on dev.

POST /api/social/media.reason: A successful POST writes the live clip map that the Instagram poster reads, with no delete route. The bad-address 400 and the 401 are checked on dev.

POST /api/social/clip/register.reason: A successful register needs a real clip uploaded to the social-clips bucket and writes the live clip map (no delete). The never-uploaded refusal is checked on dev (it answers 500; a 4xx would be better).

POST /api/social/notify.reason: Sends Mark a push/email notification. Only the 401 without a token is checked.

POST /api/social/schedule-config.reason: Overwrites the live posting times; there is no fixture copy of the config and no validation path that refuses without writing (a body whose times are all malformed is SAVED as an empty list instead of refused — reported as a site problem 2026-10-08). Only the 401 is checked.

POST /api/groups.reason: Creates a group file and there is no delete route for groups, so a fixture group could never be removed. The missing-name and card-number 400s and the 401 are checked on dev (ops.group-writes-refuse). Needs DELETE /api/groups/:id (or an archive flag) for a fixture.

PATCH /api/groups/:id.reason: Changes a real group (no fixture group is possible without a delete route). Empty edit 400, card-number 400, unknown group 404 and 401 are checked on dev.

POST /api/groups/:id/payment-schedule.reason: Inserts payment rows into a real group's file. The unknown-group 404 is checked on dev; a success needs a fixture group (see POST /api/groups).

POST /api/groups/intake.reason: A real upload stores a PDF in the group-docs bucket and has it read by the paid model, with no delete route. No-file and not-a-PDF 400s and the 401 are checked on dev.

POST /api/groups/intake/:id/retry.reason: Re-runs the paid model reader on a stored document. Unknown-intake 404 and already-accepted 409 are checked on dev.

POST /api/groups/intake/:id/accept.reason: Creates a group file (no delete route). Unknown-intake 404 and already-accepted 409 are checked on dev.

PUT /api/groups/:id/marketing/answers.reason: Overwrites a real group's marketing interview. The unknown-group 404 and the 401 are checked on dev; a success needs a fixture group.

POST /api/groups/:id/marketing/write.reason: Writes copy with a paid model call and takes the group's live page down until re-approved. The unknown-group 404 and the 401 are checked on dev.

PUT /api/groups/:id/marketing/copy.reason: Overwrites a real group's page copy (and can take the page down). The unknown-group 404 is checked on dev.

POST /api/groups/:id/marketing/approve.reason: Takes a real group page live or down. The unknown-group 404 and the 401 are checked on dev; a success needs a fixture group with clean copy.

PATCH /api/groups/:id/interests/:rowId.reason: Needs a real reply row, and the only way to create one is the public interest form, which e-mails Mark. Unknown-status 400, unknown-reply 404 and 401 are checked on dev.

POST /api/group-page/:code/interest.reason: A successful reply is stored as a lead and e-mails Mark (priority lead); Turnstile is not enforced on dev. The malformed-code 404, the bot honeypot (accepted, nothing stored) and the no-name/no-email 400 are checked on dev, with the reply count proven unchanged.
